title: First 30-Day Activation Plan — Crestline Health POC
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the operational playbook for Crestline Health’s 30-day POC focused on clinical documentation assist and nurse triage summarization. Goal is to demonstrate a production-like integration of Redwood Inference hosted API with Crestline’s EMR-driven workflow and validate cost, latency, and clinical accuracy guardrails.

POC Objectives (measurable):
- Integrate Redwood hosted API into Crestline staging environment and process 1,000 representative triage notes within the 30-day window.
- Achieve median inference latency <= 350ms for 512-token requests across 95% of calls.
- Maintain generation-level ROUGE-L >= 0.72 against Crestline gold summaries on the sample set.
- Keep per-inference incremental cost below $0.003 (token-normalized) under test traffic profile.
- Prove secure handling: no PHI persists in logs beyond 24 hours; KMS encryption verified in dedicated test run.

Acceptance Criteria (pass/fail gates):
- Functional: API calls succeed for 99% of test runs (retries excluded).
- Quality: On the held-out evaluation set, extractive/abstractive metrics meet thresholds above. Clinical SME sign-off on 30 random samples.
- Performance: SLOs met as measured in Redwood Console traces for a continuous 48-hour window at 50rps.
- Security & Compliance: Pen test checklist items 1–6 cleared and audit log showing KMS-wrapped keys for model requests.

Key Stakeholders and Responsibilities:
- Redwood: Maya Patel (POC lead) — overall coordination, rollout decisions, demo.
- Redwood: Samir Banerjee — integration engineer, API wiring and sample harness.
- Redwood: Olivia Gomez — observability & cost instrumentation, dashboards.
- Crestline: Jared Kline — clinical informatics lead (primary contact).
- Crestline: Dr. Elena Rivera — clinical SME for quality sign-off.

High-Level 30-Day Timeline (week-by-week milestones):
Week 0 (pre-day 1): provisioning and security
- Validate Crestline VPC peering or IP allowlist, exchange API keys, complete KMS test vectors.
- Deliver minimal test dataset (500 de-identified triage notes).

Week 1 (days 1–7): integration + smoke tests
- Day 1–2: Redwood provides SDK snippet and sample serverless connector.
- Day 3–4: Crestline devs wire API into staging; run 100 synthetic calls.
- Day 5–7: Run initial 24h load test at 5rps, sanity checks, collect first latency profile.

Week 2 (days 8–14): focused quality evaluation
- Execute evaluation harness: metric collection (ROUGE, BLEU, factuality heuristics).
- Clinical SME review session at day 12 with 30 sampled outputs; log issues and false-positive patterns.

Week 3 (days 15–21): scale and cost modeling
- Increase test load to 50rps and run continuous 48h window.
- Olivia to publish cost per request breakdown and token distribution chart.
- Verify batching/kv-cache configuration suggestions from Redwood Optimize to reduce per-token cost.

Week 4 (days 22–30): decision & handoff
- Final acceptance run and executive demo.
- Capture runbooks for Dedicated or Private deployment if Crestline requests.
- Postmortem + decision meeting on day 30: go/no-go, list of production gaps.

Workshop Agenda (kickoff & technical working session — 90 minutes):
- 0–10m: Intro, goals, success metrics (Maya + Jared)
- 10–30m: Architecture walkthrough (Samir) — data flow, auth, network requirements
- 30–50m: Demo of sample harness and test dataset (Olivia)
- 50–70m: Clinical review protocol and labeling guide (Dr. Rivera)
- 70–85m: Risk register and mitigation (all)
- 85–90m: Next steps and action items assignment

Integration Checklist (minimum viable integration):
- API keys provisioned and rotated using Crestline key vault (timestamped).
- TLS mutual auth validated or IP allowlist confirmed.
- Minimal adapter in staging to transform Crestline note JSON -> Redwood API payload.
- Idempotency keys and request tracing headers inserted by Crestline.
- Server-side logging masked (PHI redaction heuristic applied) and log TTL set to 24h.

Evaluation Methodology and Artifacts to Produce:
- Collate 1,000 test notes: 700 train/holdout split for iterative tuning, 300 final evaluation.
- Produce a quantitative report: latency percentiles, token histograms, cost per invocation, ROUGE/BERTScore/Factuality heuristics.
- Clinical sign-off doc containing sampled notes, SME comments, and remediation recommendations.

Risk Register (top 6):
1) Data leakage in logs — Mitigation: immediate log TTL, mask layer, KMS, and audit of log pipeline.
2) Quality drift on longer notes — Mitigation: restrict input length, test quantized model variants.
3) Latency spikes under burst — Mitigation: enable burst capacity and fallback to smaller model variant.
4) Unexpected token cost from verbosity — Mitigation: apply prompt controls, max tokens, and truncation policy.
5) Regulatory review delay — Mitigation: prioritize security checklist items and tag demos for compliance review.
6) SME availability for sign-off — Mitigation: schedule multiple candidate review windows in week 2.

Decision Gates and Criteria for Next Steps:
- Green: All acceptance criteria met and Crestline opts for Dedicated or hosted production path.
- Amber: Quality or cost shortfall identified and a 30-day remediation plan accepted.
- Red: Critical security concern or systemic quality failure — pause and engage legal/compliance.

Operational Runbook Notes (quick ops play):
- If error rate >1% for 2 consecutive hours, scale to burst and enable fallback model. Notify SRE on-call.
- For latency P95 breach, temporarily reduce batching window, increase worker concurrency and run tracing.

Sample API Tests (to be run by Crestline devs):
1) Sanity: POST /v1/generate with 3 short notes, expect 200, median latency < 200ms in dev.
2) Load: sustained 50rps for 48h, collect p50/p95/p99.
3) Edge: notes with >1,200 tokens, verify truncation policy and stable behavior.
4) Security: malformed payloads, injection attempts logged and rejected with 4xx/429 as configured.

Reporting and Artifacts Delivery:
- Weekly progress email every Friday with: run counts, latency/cost deltas, open issues, SME notes.
- Deliver final POC pack: evaluation report, runbook, production migration checklist, and raw debug traces (obfuscated).

Open Questions (to resolve in kickoff):
- Which Crestline environment will host the adapter (hosted staging vs on-prem staging)?
- Are there redaction rules specific to Crestline beyond default PHI heuristics?
- What is the expected QPS at go-live baseline for cost modeling?

Notes / Quick to-dos (first 48 hours):
- Redwood: send staging API key and SDK snippet (Samir).
- Crestline: share 500 de-identified notes and nominate SME interview times (Jared).
- Olivia: provision dashboard template in Redwood Console and share link.

Appendix: example acceptance checklist (short)
- [ ] API connectivity (OK)
- [ ] 1,000 notes processed (OK/NA)
- [ ] Latency SLO validated (OK/NA)
